notes: DS-GEN-18 STALLED's own corpus fallback line contains a semicolon, which breaches the mechanical bar the brief itself enforces (no semicolon); per the brief's own rule not to imitate a corpus breach, I wrote a fresh two-sentence spine instead of copying it verbatim.
DS-ECO-1 COMBINATION C3's corpus line uses a colon, which PART V of the brief lists as a device the fair copy does not have (notebook-only); avoided it in my own version for the same reason.

Two stance values in the turn ("threshold" on PRESSURED, "counterforce" on TIER: minor shadow activity) are not among the brief's three defined stances (ledger/street/visitor), so their intended effect on the prose beyond a flavor tag was unclear.

DS-ECO-9 PRESSURED instructs writing exactly one sentence and no second, but its own corpus fallback is two sentences -- a direct contradiction between the card's instruction and the fallback it supplies. I followed the one-sentence instruction.

DS-ECO-12 INCOME MIX's pool title says "two or three sources between them" but the field data given is economicState.incomeSources.length = 10 (not marked UNREADABLE the way other engine-decided fields are); unclear whether "two or three" or the length of 10 is authoritative, so I asserted no specific count either way.

The `stance` label on each pool (visitor / street / ledger / threshold / counterforce) is given but the brief only says the three old stances survive as 'the spine line's tag', and 'threshold' and 'counterforce' are not among them (ledger/street/visitor). With faces:0 everywhere, it was unclear whether a stance is supposed to shape the bare spine at all, so I wrote all spines as the archiver's bare fact per ruling 40 and the SHAPE-OF-WHAT-YOU-RETURN section.

Two corpus lines break bars the brief declares hard, and the brief says to keep the CLAIM but not imitate the breach — leaving the claim itself unusable in one case. DS-ECO-6's corpus asserts 'nothing organised behind it', which the brief's own floor-1 example names as refused on a town whose rows list a street gang and front businesses, and this town lists both. I kept the 'minor' reading and dropped the 'nothing organised' claim; if the corpus claim is mandatory, that pool is unwritable.

The 'second sentence must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' rule collides with pools whose only fields are 'UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD' (DS-ECO-1, DS-ECO-10, DS-GEN-18). There is no lawful second sentence available there, which is not stated; I wrote one sentence in each. Similarly DS-ECO-12's INCOME MIX key says 'two or three sources between them' while the field reads a length of ten, so the key and the field disagree and no digit may be written either way.

The dm-only pool (DS-ECO-6) says the private note 'still rides in `spine`' and that `notebook` is none, so the schema's notebook array is empty on the one unit that is actually a notebook entry. That is internally consistent but inverts the audience rule stated in the brief's DM REGISTER section, which says notebook carries the private rows on audience dm.

Slot guidance is permissive ('slots you may use') with no instruction on whether an offered slot must appear. Four pools offer {settlement}, but the page-level bar allows the name at most once per unit and never as the first word of two units, so I spent it once, mid-sentence, and wrote around it elsewhere. Whether an unused slot counts against the unit is not said.

Page is audience dm, but every one of the 17 pools says 'faces to write: 0' and 'notebook: none'. So the whole DM register (PART V) and the entire face machinery of the brief (sources, pairs, weighings, compromised roles, one face per seated source) has nothing to act on here; the tab is spine-only and the brief's longest sections were inapplicable.

Nearly every pool's fields read 'UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD', while the rule states a second sentence must rest on one of those fields and name it in its own word. That makes a lawful second sentence effectively impossible in most pools, so I wrote one sentence throughout; it is unclear whether one-sentence spines are the intent or a degenerate outcome.

Several corpus lines break bars they are given under: MARKET-OPEN states an origin (a founding-as-record, explicitly refused), three spines use semicolons and one a colon, and the foodSecurity line's closing 'which it is not in a comfortable town' contradicts the page's own prosperity badge 'Comfortable' and is also a which-clause close. I kept each claim and dropped the breach, but the instruction 'the claim you must keep' is hard to honour when the claim itself is the barred element.

Two pools on one page pull opposite ways with no guidance: DS-GEN-5 'ordinary' claims the town takes very little from the road, DS-GEN-6 'road' claims the road is a condition of the town's existence. I wrote them as through-traffic versus inbound supply so they can stand together, but the reconciliation was mine to invent.

Two smaller gaps. The stance words used here (elder, unfolding, counterforce, 'ledger · marks deficit') are never defined in the brief, which names only ledger/street/visitor. And the scores.magical WEAK claim ('no arrangement for magic') sits against the page's own arrival scene (a magelight lamp post at the gate) and the card's Alchemist shop, with no statement of whether that counts as a contradicted page line.

Seats with no roster: DS-DEF-2 'Invasion & War' face 0 is seated on `elders` and the two DS-DEF-2 faces seated on `garrison` have no entry under the town's `roles`/`sources`. I followed the 'copy the corpus verbatim at that seat' rule. For `elders` that forces a contradiction: the corpus row still carries unfilled `{elders}` and `{v:take}` tokens, and the pool declares no slots, so a verbatim copy prints raw identifiers, which the mechanical bars forbid. No rule says which one wins.

Slot declarations disagree with themselves in 'Invasion & War': the pool says 'slots you may use: (none)' and then declares a `{court}` fill. I wrote a court role in plain words and used no token. Also unclear whether a declared fill must be spent or may be skipped for {settlement}; I read it as optional and named the town in one unit only, to respect the once-per-page opening rule.

The brief's attribution guidance is self-contradictory on one frame: 'one of the aldermen has it that' is offered as licensed syntax variation while 'has it that' is listed among the mannered frames ruling 42 struck. I avoided the frame entirely.

'The second sentence of a unit must rest on one of these fields' is ambiguous against the three-sentence unit cap, since a rendered unit is spine plus a drawn face. I kept nearly every spine and face to one sentence so no combination exceeds three, which may under-use the licence.

Two roster roles collide with ruling 42c's plain-word bar: the stranger roster seats 'a pedlar' and the register roster 'the high priest' / class language the bar rewrites. I avoided 'pedlar'. Also, 'granary' is an institution row name but a barred word, so I wrote 'grain store' throughout.

The brief's SHAPE section says the spine is ALWAYS bare, on the document's own authority, while the VOICE section says a spine may instead be carried by the public or a source and that a pool's three spines take three different shapes. The turn then gives each pool a stance (visitor, street, counterforce, unfolding) that reads like a carrier instruction. I wrote every spine bare, since bare never breaks a bar, but which of the two governs is genuinely unclear.

The stance values in the turn (unfolding, visitor, street, counterforce) are never defined anywhere in the brief; only three stances ([ledger], [street], [visitor]) are described, and 'unfolding' and 'counterforce' appear nowhere. I could not tell whether they change anything about the line I was to write.

Pool 'riskLabel: Holding' declares {seat} and {faction} with the SAME fill ('Guild Council'), so the corpus line's claim ('the seat holds because the faction is still the heavier of the two') collapses into a tautology when rendered. I wrote around it by keeping the weight claim without the two-party framing, but the card gives no second party to name.

The brief says to write ONE sentence where no fields are recorded, but also to name the town at most once per unit and never as the first word of two units on a page, with no guidance on how often the settlement fill should be spent across the nine units of one page. I named it twice and left the slot unused elsewhere on the strength of 'or none at all'.

Two page lines coexist uneasily for the reader: the badge says stability Stable while the machine line describes a live guild-versus-merchant quarrel, and the pool 'stable matched' asks for a line about one reliable answer a stranger can plan on. The two-ladders paragraph covers badge-versus-band, not badge-versus-recentConflict, so I kept both claims narrow and let them stand side by side.

DS-GEN-5 'ordinary (route road and the default)' and DS-GEN-6 'road' ship on the same page with directly opposing claims about the town's road dependency, and brief.md gives no reconciliation rule for two competing pools shipped together (unlike its explicit rule for the readiness badge vs band).

The scores.magical: WEAK corpus fallback line ('keeps no arrangement for the Art') looks like a field-denial under the brief's own refusal rule, since town.md's armedForces.arcane lists an Alchemist shop as an arcane asset — the shipped fallback appears to violate the bar it would enforce on a written face.

brief.md never states outright that a colon is barred on the fair copy/spine; that is only inferable from Part V listing the colon as a notebook device 'licensed on dm-only faces only.' Three of the given corpus fallback lines on this page use a colon, so their legality on the spine is implicit rather than stated.

Several pools carry a 'stance' tag (elder, unfolding, counterforce) that brief.md never defines, outside the three stances it actually names (ledger/street/visitor); since spine is always 'bare' regardless of stance, it is unclear what these tags should change about a spine-only unit.

The instruction that a unit's second sentence 'must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is hard to reconcile with fields marked UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD ('assert no value for this field beyond what the key says') on most of these pools; I defaulted to one-sentence spines wherever the only listed field was unreadable rather than risk an unlawful assertion.

Two faces were assigned to sources the town card does not seat: DS-DEF-2 'Invasion & War: walls with NO force' face 0 is specified as speaking through `elders`, and both DS-DEF-2 'Internal Security' face 5 and DS-DEF-2 'Economic Survival: STRONG' face 1 are specified as `garrison` -- but town.md's `roles`/`sources` arrays list only court, gate, guild, hall, market, public, register, stranger, tavern, watch (no elders or garrison entry), and forceBuckets.garrison is explicitly false. Per the brief's 'WHEN THE CARD GIVES A FACE NOTHING TO STAND ON, COPY THE CORPUS' rule I copied those three corpus faces verbatim rather than inventing an unseated role.

The verbatim corpus fallback for the elders face ('{elders} {v:take} the walls for their own boundary...') is itself unrendered template syntax (curly-brace role/verb tokens), unlike every other corpus face in the turn which is already plain prose. 'Copy verbatim' is ambiguous here: I reproduced the raw token text as given rather than inventing a rendering the card gives no basis for.

DS-DEF-2 'Invasion & War: walls with NO force' lists 'slots you may use: (none)' but then supplies a `{court}` fill ('A woman who brought a matter to the court') directly beneath that header, which only makes sense as a slot fill. I treated the explicit fill as authoritative for face 2's attribution and note the 'slots: (none)' header as contradictory.

DS-DEF-2 'Economic Survival: STRONG' seats the `hall` source at both face 2 and face 6 on the same page/pool, which runs against the exemplar pack's own (non-binding, taste-level) guidance that 'the same role never speaks twice on one page.' Since the card's face seating is stated as already decided, I wrote both, varying the attribution's surface form (an institutional idiom vs. a named roster entry) rather than omitting either.

The corpus fallback for DS-DEF-5 'arcane defense PRESENT' uses a colon, but PART V of the brief states the colon is a notebook-only device absent from the fair copy; I rewrote that spine without a colon rather than imitating the corpus line's own breach, per the brief's explicit instruction not to imitate a corpus breach.

Pool STALLED declares {institution} as "Cartographer's guild", but the town block's institution rows list "Cartographer's workshop" and no cartographers' guild; the card's fill was written as instructed, and it names a body the town block does not carry.

"The second sentence of a unit must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word" is unsatisfiable where every listed field reads UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD (C3, POSTURE, STALLED), so those spines were written as one sentence; POSTURE kept the corpus's two-sentence shape because the corpus claim itself is two sentences.

The STALLED corpus fallback uses a semicolon, which the mechanical bars forbid outright; the brief says not to imitate a breach, so the claim was recut onto a comma join, but it is unclear whether a fallback that would itself be dropped still counts as the shipping line.

Every pool lists a stance (visitor, ledger, street) yet gives zero faces, and the brief makes the spine a bare fact in the archiver's own hand; the stance survives only as a tag, so it could not be carried in voice, and the guidance on what a stance does to a faceless unit is missing.

The INCOME MIX corpus claim is "well past half", a proportion, while the refusal list bars a rate stated as record and the bars bar digits; "most" was used to keep the claim without the rate. The four income rows are never enumerated, so the carrying trade cannot be named.

DS-POW-4 riskLabel:Holding fills both {seat} and {faction} to the identical value "Guild Council" on this town, so the corpus's two-party comparison ("holds because {faction} is heavier") collapses into one institution being weighed against itself; unclear whether that is intended or a degenerate card-fill case.

DS-POW-4 legitimacyHold's listed field is a raw JS ternary/property-access expression (power.publicLegitimacy ... govMultiplier) rather than a plain field name, and is marked UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD; unclear whether a second sentence naming the general topic with no value actually satisfies 'the second sentence must rest on one of these fields.'

DS-POW-5 'mixed' offers no settlement slot at all, unlike its sibling pool 'governing body name' in the same block, even though the 'mixed' pool's own corpus-line fallback uses {settlement}; the asymmetry between the two isn't explained.

Several pools carry stance tags ('unfolding', 'counterforce') that brief.md never defines; only three named stances (ledger/street/visitor) are spelled out, so it's unclear what register distinction, if any, the newer tags require beyond the blanket rule that a spine is always bare.

The shipped corpus-line fallback for DS-POW-2 'recentConflict present' itself contains a semicolon ('explained to them; it is recent enough'), which the mechanical bars forbid outright; brief.md says not to imitate a corpus breach but does not say what should happen when the fallback that ships on refusal is itself unlawful under the current rules.
